requested_by: campaign coordinator, mandatory preflight before Wave 3
assumption_chosen: A role read from morphological case standing beside a finite verb, scoped to one metrical pada (Rigveda) or one sentence (DCS chapters with no parse), is the role a dependency parse would assign to that token.
why_this_one_carries_the_most_weight: 28,370 of 30,274 assertions -- 93.7% -- get their roles this way, including every Rigvedic assertion and every Samavedic projection. It is also the assumption behind the two figures the report leads with: the 0 to 5,219 three-slot count and the 91.9% unrepresentable-filler cost. The Samavedic identity projection (372 assertions) and the dominant-sense rule (1,139) are both smaller by an order of magnitude, and both are already labelled and filterable on the row.
why_a_test_was_possible_when_the_report_: The report's claim was that no independent witness exists, and that is true of the SOURCE. It is false of the RULE. 2,823 DCS sentences carry a human-validated dependency parse, so the case rule can be run on exactly those sentences and scored against the parse, token by token. The instrument has a ground truth even where the corpus does not. Not seeing that was a gap in the original evaluation design, and it is recorded here as such.
method: For every DCS sentence carrying a parse, with the deployed single-finite-verb gate applied and the predicate resolved by the same root map: extract roles twice -- once from the verb's dependency children (the deployed TREEBANK_DEPREL path) and once from morphological case over the whole sentence (the deployed MORPHOLOGY_RULE_CASE path) -- and compare per token id. Every disagreement is then classified by walking the token's head chain, so the three unlike kinds of disagreement are never averaged into one number.
expected_before_running: The single-finite-verb gate was expected to hold the error down, since it already suppresses non-agent roles wherever two finite verbs share a scope. Precision was expected in the 0.85 to 0.95 band.

probe_1_raw.assumption_under_test: A role read from morphological case standing beside a finite verb, scoped to one pada (Rigveda) or one sentence (unparsed DCS), is the role a dependency parse would assign. 28,370 of 30,274 assertions rest on it.
probe_1_raw.method: Run the deployed case rule on the DCS sentences that DO carry a parse, with the deployed single-finite-verb gate applied, and score every filler it emits against the treebank role for the same token.

verdict.headline: FAILS AT FILLER LEVEL, HOLDS AT ASSERTION LEVEL
verdict.filler_level: Raw precision 0.4855, far below the 0.85-0.95 expected. Decomposed: 623 of 2,715 emitted fillers (23.0%) are attached across a clause boundary and 50 carry the wrong role, so 24.8% are wrong. A further 580 (21.4%) are a second token inside a single argument -- a determiner, adjective, apposition or conjunct -- which inflates the count without changing the role, and 406 of the 423 checkable ones carry the same role as the argument head they sit in.
verdict.the_gate_does_not_catch_it: The gate counts FINITE verbs. The leakage comes from non-finite clauses -- acl 75, xcomp:result 56, xcomp 34, advcl 42 -- and from subjects internal to a nominal, nsubj 106. The gate is blind to all of them, so the mitigation the report relied on does not cover the failure mode.
verdict.assertion_level_holds: Predicates, frames, passage counts and every abstention count derive from the verb's own morphology and are untouched by scope. The one headline figure that does depend on fillers, the agent-predicate-patient triple, survives at 0.922 -- and the residual error is conservative: the parse finds 42 complete triples the case rule missed against 17 it manufactured, so the rule UNDER-reports completeness.
verdict.cost_figure_holds: Deity share is 7.74% among parse-confirmed fillers and 3.72% among parse-rejected ones, so leakage is less deity-heavy than genuine attachment. Discarding every rejected filler would move the overall deity share from 8.08% to about 8.6%. The 91.9% figure stands and the conclusion is, if anything, understated.

figures_that_move: None of the counts in the artifact. Nothing was restaged or renumbered.

What moves is the confidence attached to one class of figure: a case-scoped role FILLER count now carries a measured 24.8% wrong-attachment rate and a 21.4% duplication rate, both recorded on every row's evaluation block and in manifest.evaluation.
manifest.qa.defects_found 4 -> 5 and manifest.qa.sampled 44 -> 1,158, because the preflight is a fifth finding over 1,114 mechanically scored assertions.
what_was_deliberately_not_done: No attempt to patch the rule. Cross-clause leakage cannot be detected without a parse, and all of the Rigveda plus three quarters of the non-Rigvedic material has none. Tightening the case rule by guesswork -- refusing a filler that looks like a modifier, say -- would trade a measured error for an unmeasured one. The honest move is to publish the rate and let a consumer discount or filter.
the_sixth_case_the_owner_asked_us_to_loo: This is a modelling error on our side of the line, not a source absence: DCS supplied a dependency parse for these sentences all along and the rule that reads them ignored it wherever the sentence fell outside the parsed quarter. The pattern matches the five prior cases -- the refusal was correct in form and the ATTACHMENT was wrong -- with the difference that here the wrong attachment is inside a verse rather than between verses, so no coverage count could ever have shown it.
